Playbook.name: Windows — Remote SAM Enumeration via SMB Named Pipe - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A remote client accessed the samr named pipe over SMB (5145, RelativeTargetName samr), excluding known scanners and machine accounts - remote SAM/account enumeration (SharpHound/net commands). Triage question: is an actor enumerating accounts for attack planning, or an unlisted legitimate tool?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Remote SAM enumeration maps users and groups for privilege-escalation and lateral-movement targeting - a recon step before the attack.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the SAM enumeration is hostile account discovery or an unlisted legitimate tool.

Step.name: Who enumerated, from where, and how broadly
Step.Purpose: A source enumerating SAM on many hosts is doing recon; a single admin query differs.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "5145" AND winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName == "samr" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS accesses = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list = VALUES(host.name) BY src, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT accesses DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One source enumerating SAM across many hosts = recon sweep (SharpHound-style). A single access by an admin tool to one host may be benign. Rule already excludes Nessus/manageengine/machine accounts.

Step.name: Is the same source also doing other discovery/lateral activity
Step.Purpose: SAM enumeration alongside share access or service-pipe access is an active attack chain.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "5145" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName IN ("svcctl","atsvc","PSEXESVC","lsarpc","netlogon") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), pipes = VALUES(winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Access to service-control (svcctl) or lsarpc pipes alongside samr indicates enumeration + lateral-execution tooling - escalate.

Node.Condition: One source enumerating SAM across multiple hosts, or combined with service-pipe access.
Node.Result: True Positive (Account Enumeration Recon - escalate, investigate source)

Node.Condition: A single access by an unlisted but legitimate admin/inventory tool.
SAM access from a source whose role is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SAMR-WHO, INV-02-SAMR-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the tool; add to the exclusion; close as false_positive.
Investigate the source host for the enumeration tool; open IR.
Scope what it mapped; watch for follow-on targeting.

Indicators.Item: A known tool per a broken config.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
